ownFindingsDuringThisPass.what: the survivor control fired on a green local selection, reporting a bare process id
ownFindingsDuringThisPass.diagnosis: The finding named a number. By the time it was read the process was gone and nothing said what had leaked, so it could not be judged at all.
ownFindingsDuringThisPass.action: The finding carries the command line now, and that is a case of its own.

ownFindingsDuringThisPass.what: with the command line, the survivor was VBCSCompiler
ownFindingsDuringThisPass.diagnosis: The shared Roslyn compiler server, which the SDK keeps alive on purpose so the next build reuses it. It is shared with every build on the machine and holds nothing of the run: no fixture port, no file under the run root, no broker.
ownFindingsDuringThisPass.action: Excluded by name, not by a longer wait - its idle timeout is longer than any grace period this runner could sensibly have, so waiting would have turned a false finding into a slow one. A process of the run's own tree that is not that server is still a survivor, and both halves have a case and a mutation.

ownFindingsDuringThisPass.what: a long background run was killed with the tool call that launched it
ownFindingsDuringThisPass.diagnosis: nohup only ignores SIGHUP; a process group kill still reaches the job, and the launching call hit its own timeout after five of seven categories.
ownFindingsDuringThisPass.action: Long runs are started in a session of their own now. This is my tooling, not the product; no repository state was affected and no process was left behind.

notRun: The full repository gate, which the directive forbids until it approves one.
rabbitmq, sql-transport and entity-framework-core: each still needs one complete clean run to record its expected identity set, and until then a receipt covering it says so instead of passing.
